scope: Same-connection registry uniqueness and provider association, explicit control binding, safe withdrawal and fresh auxiliary recovery

contract.registry: Own wl_registry and asynchronous sync on existing public Qt Wayland display/default queue; no new connection or server
contract.association: desktop_global event carries management global name visible for this wl_client; 0 means invisible
contract.binding: Explicit generated protocol binding to inventoried control ID; no QWaylandClientExtension for that control
contract.resume: Completed unique compatible inventory, matching association, availability and fresh serial/ack required
contract.lateInventory: New revision required after timeout; late inventory cannot resume automatically
contract.duplicateControl: Pause own existing connection, preserve bound ID; restore unique topology with fresh confirmation
contract.duplicateKdeManagement: Process-lifetime restartRequired latch; requires new auxiliary, not a new controller object
contract.withdrawal: Missing or conflicting provider permits pause/exit; known local views/popups hidden before returning to dispatch
contract.briefWithdrawal: Only bwmControlWithdrawn view marker permits restore of same view before queued teardown
contract.retiredControls: userdata=null until client destroy/disconnect; in-flight requests inert, no ack/activation
contract.legacyV1: Previous barrier supported without new event; current host requires v2

assertions: Unique management/control pair and declared association verified before resume
Duplicate control blocks resume while permitting pause and recovery on the same explicitly bound resource
Available foreign test control declaring management name zero is rejected despite compatible version counts
Late initial registry inventory remains unavailable until a fresh revision
Duplicate KDE management latches restart requirement but does not trap pause/exit
New controller in the same process cannot reset the private KDE backend
Original VirtualDesktopInfo sees zero after duplicate removal; fresh Qt child sees four on the second inherited fixture endpoint
Two v1 clients retain cancellation/isolation/rebind semantics
Requests in flight to retired controls do not acknowledge or produce invalid_object
Offscreen Qt test restores the same view marked withdrawn without restoring a manual hide
